subject: Re: Model regression after v2.1.3 rollout / next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-15T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Follow-up: model fit recommendations and next steps

Hi Alex —

Thanks again for the time earlier today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our discovery: 

- Primary goal: replace rule-based ticket summarization with an LLM-backed extracted summary + suggested actions. Target latency < 500ms P95 for 1-2k concurrent users.
- Data constraints: customer PII must never be logged to third-party telemetry; you need VPC/private deployment for sensitive queues.
- Recommended starting models: rwd-3b-std (good latency/cost balance) and rwd-7b-ht for higher-quality summaries.
- Suggested evaluation set: attached prompt_set_v2.jsonl (30 representative tickets + edge cases) and our benchmark sheet eval_benchmarks_ACME.xlsx.

Next steps:
1) Dylan to run a quick eval of rwd-3b-std vs rwd-7b-ht on the attached prompt set and send top failure modes. (Dylan: can you target EOD Thursday?)
2) If results look good, we’ll propose a canary rollout on a small percentage of traffic and pin model version for ACME.
3) I'll open a SOC and contract checklist for VPC/private deployment (Priya on our side will own the compliance pack).

I attached the prompt set and benchmarks we discussed. Let me know if anything is missing.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

Attachments: prompt_set_v2.jsonl, eval_benchmarks_ACME.xlsx

Thanks Marissa — appreciate the follow-up and the assets. Quick update from our side: after we integrated the hosted API yesterday for a small test slice, we noticed a meaningful change in output quality compared to earlier runs. Two quick examples I pasted below where the newer responses hallucinated policy steps and omitted critical customer details.

Example 1 (ticket id 87421): expected concise summary + issue type; got a longer speculative troubleshooting checklist that references internal tooling we don’t use.
Example 2 (ticket id 87433): summary dropped an SLA breach flag.

These align with what our support leads reported this morning — cohesion and factuality seem degraded. We suspect this coincides with the v2.1.3 rollout you mentioned on your status page. Can you confirm which model variant we were routed to and whether we can pin us to the prior version while you investigate?

We need to avoid regressions in production; if this is a behavior change in the model, we’ll need a rollback or a pinned route immediately. Also happy to share more examples — Sara can drop a short spreadsheet of failing cases.

— Alex
Product Ops Lead, Acme Corp
alex.johnson@acme.com
